source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
notes: Next on the agenda are alternating forms. In the indicative mood we have two alternating tense forms: past imperfect and pluperfect episodic. Consider, for instance, past imperfect in (52). (52a) gives the full, auxiliated form which has the same structure as pluperfect except that the Part node is associated with the [aorist] feature. (52b) gives the reduced form, without the auxiliary e-.
